new_task_1.title: Restrict config-install archives to zip and tar-based formats
new_task_1.description: Conan 2.17.0 narrows `conan config install` archive handling so configuration archives are extracted only from ZIP files and tar-based compressed formats. Plain `.gz` inputs are no longer treated as installable configuration archives.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan config install` only recognizes and extracts supported archive containers for configuration installation, and no longer accepts a standalone `.gz` file as a compressed config source.

expectation.grounded: The config installer must keep extracting `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tbz2`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`, and `.txz` inputs. Archive detection for config install must no longer classify plain `.gz` files as supported compressed configuration archives, and the install flow must stop relying on the generic unzip helper branch that previously decompressed a single-file `.gz` payload.
expectation.conceptual: Configuration install sources should be actual archive containers that can unpack a configuration tree, not arbitrary gzip-compressed single files.

constraints.grounded: Existing config-install behavior for ZIP and tar-based archives must remain intact, including extraction into the temporary install folder before copying configuration contents into the Conan home. The change should be limited to archive-type recognition and extraction handling for config install inputs.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should tighten accepted archive formats without changing how valid multi-file configuration archives are installed.

behavior: `conan config install` continues to extract ZIP archives as configuration sources.
`conan config install` continues to extract tar-based configuration archives, including `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tbz2`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`, and `.txz`.
A standalone `.gz` file is no longer recognized as a supported compressed config-install input.
Config-install archive extraction now uses ZIP-specific extraction for ZIP files and tar extraction for tar-based formats instead of the older generic helper path that also handled plain `.gz`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan config install` with a ZIP configuration archive, the configuration should still be extracted and installed successfully.
When a user runs `conan config install` with a tar-based configuration archive such as `.tar.gz` or `.txz`, the configuration should still be extracted and installed successfully.
When a user provides a plain `.gz` file to `conan config install`, Conan should no longer treat it as a supported compressed configuration archive.
When valid ZIP or tar-based configuration archives are installed, the rest of the config installation flow should behave as before.

new_task_2.title: Warn and fall back to config mode for CMakeDeps2 module requests
new_task_2.description: Conan 2.17.0 makes `CMakeDeps2` explicitly warn when a dependency requests `cmake_find_mode=module`, because that generator does not support module mode and will proceed using config-mode generation instead.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `CMakeDeps2` surfaces unsupported `cmake_find_mode=module` settings clearly and continues with config-mode generation instead of silently pretending to honor module mode.

expectation.grounded: During `CMakeDeps2` generation, if a dependency declares `cmake_find_mode` equal to `module`, Conan must emit a warning stating that CMakeConfigDeps does not support module find mode for that dependency and that config mode will be used regardless. Generation should continue instead of skipping the dependency or failing.
expectation.conceptual: Users configuring the new CMake deps generator should be told when module mode is unsupported, and Conan should make the fallback behavior explicit rather than silent.

constraints.grounded: Dependencies with `cmake_find_mode=none` must continue to be skipped as before, and dependencies using supported modes must continue through normal generation. This change should add the warning and explicit fallback only for the unsupported module-mode case.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should clarify unsupported configuration without broadening module-mode support or changing normal config-mode generation.

behavior: When `CMakeDeps2` encounters a dependency with `cmake_find_mode=module`, Conan emits a deprecation-tagged warning for that dependency.
The warning states that module find mode is not supported by CMakeConfigDeps and that config mode will be used instead.
Generation continues after the warning, using config-mode behavior rather than failing or generating module-mode files.
Dependencies configured with other supported find modes continue to behave as before.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency sets `self.cpp_info.set_property("cmake_find_mode", "module")` and a consumer installs with `-g CMakeDeps` using the new generator flow, Conan should print a warning that module find mode is unsupported.
When that warning is emitted, the install or generation flow should still complete instead of aborting solely because of the unsupported module mode.
When a dependency uses `cmake_find_mode=none`, Conan should continue skipping generation for that dependency as before.
When a dependency uses normal supported config-mode generation, this upgrade should not change its output behavior.
